Q357.L1t: Deserts are dry regions found on several continents, where little rain falls and few plants and animals can live.
Q357.L2t: The passage says the size and location of the world's deserts have always shifted over millions of years as climates change and mountains rise.
Q357.L3t: The passage says humans are the greatest cause of recent desert growth, then spends most of its length describing what countries such as Iran, Algeria, the USSR and India do to stop deserts from spreading.
Q357.L4t: The passage as a whole is about people acting to hold back and control the spread of deserts.
Q357.L2f: The passage says the world's deserts have stayed the same size and in the same places for millions of years.
Q357.L3f: The passage is mostly a description of what a desert looks and feels like, and the later paragraphs on human action are only brief side remarks.
Q357.L4f: The best statement of the main idea is that deserts are lands of silence and space.

Q761.L1t: The Edinburgh Festival is a large yearly arts event held in the Scottish capital each summer.
Q761.L2t: The festival was started in 1947 by a group of famous people from the art world led by an Austrian conductor.
Q761.L3t: The passage says the idea behind founding the festival in 1947, just after the Second World War, was to reunite Europe through music, dance and theatre.
Q761.L4t: The festival was started in order to bring the countries of Europe together again after the war.
Q761.L2f: The festival was first organised in 1947 by a committee of Scottish university students who wanted a summer event in Edinburgh.
Q761.L3f: The passage says the festival was set up in 1947 mainly as a memorial for the soldiers and war heroes who had died in the Second World War.
Q761.L4f: The festival was started in order to honour the heroes of the Second World War.

Q365.L1t: Shopping in the United States has gone through several stages, from small family shops to supermarkets, malls, superstores and online stores.
Q365.L2t: Superstores such as Wal-Mart, Office Depot and Toys "R" Us are large chain stores that have been built in many places in the United States.
Q365.L3t: The passage says that because superstores are so large, they get a big discount when they buy goods, and this lets them sell more cheaply than small stores.
Q365.L4t: Superstores can charge less because they pay less when they buy their goods.
Q365.L2f: Superstores such as Wal-Mart are small, family-owned shops that sell only a few local goods in each town.
Q365.L3f: The passage says superstores can sell cheaply because their wide spread across the whole country gives them lower costs than any other kind of shop.
Q365.L4f: Superstores can sell at much lower prices because they have been built all across the United States.
